September 2023 NEWNEWS FRS FROM THE BOOM THE BOARDARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Ryan Davidson - Commissioner Rod Beck - Board Chairman Tom Dayley - Commissioner ADA COUNTY JAIL BOND ELECTION Ada County Commissioners voted unanimously to authorize a resolution calling for a general obligation bond election for $49M to expand the Ada County Jail. Voters in Ada County will see the question on the November 7, 2023 ballot. The last major expansion to the Ada County Jail happened in 2003. At that time the county’s population was just over 325,000 people. The county’s current population is approximately 545,000. The Community Planning Association of Southwest Idaho (COMPASS) estimates that in the next decade our population will be 600,000. Learn more about the jail expansion project. If you want to see how many inmates are in custody in real time – and how many people the county is keeping out of jail through our Pretrial, Alternative Sentencing, and Misdemeanor Probation programs, check out the Ada County Jail Population Dashboard. The jail dashboard also includes demographic information, (age/race and gender) and information on types of charges for which inmates are being held.. If passed by two-thirds of voters, the estimated tax impact for the average homeowner in Ada County would be just over $13 a year. ($3.60 per $100,000 of taxable assessed value (assessed property value less any exemptions). The Ada County Jail was originally built in the late 70s and is the largest jail in the state of Idaho. Ada County is the most populous county in Idaho. TAX IMPACT The anticipated interest rate on the proposed bond issue, based upon current market rates, is 3.87% per annum. The total amount to be repaid over the life of the bonds, based on the anticipated interest rate, is $71,665,875, consisting of $49,000,000 in principal and $22,665,875 of interest. The term of the bonds will not exceed twenty (20) years from the date of issuance. The estimated average annual cost to the taxpayer of the proposed bond is a tax of $3.60 per $100,000 of taxable assessed value, per year, based on current conditions. The total existing indebtedness of Ada County, including interest accrued, is $0.00.

2 ADA COUNTY SIGNS DOMESTIC VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH PROCLAMATION AT ANNUAL EVENT Women’s and Children’s Alliance (WCA) Event underscores the Treasure Valley-wide commitment to creating safe communities Domestic Violence affects more individuals and families than many realize. The statistics say one- in-four women, and one-in-seven men but that doesn’t include the residual effects of domestic violence - the effects it has on entire families and communities. That’s why the annual Domestic Violence Awareness Month Proclamation signed by the mayors of Ada County cities as well as Nampa and Caldwell is so meaningful. Domestic violence flourishes in the shadows. It flourishes when families and individuals keep it a secret because reporting it often feels scarier than experiencing it. The annual WCA event allows the community to say no, it’s not just your imagination, and yes, you have the right to live without fear. Law enforcement personnel from around the Treasure Valley as well as supporters and friends were invited to attend the September 29th event at the Idaho Peace Officers Memorial in Meridian. Distinguished speakers included Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck, Ada County Paramedics Chief Shawn Rayne, WCA CEO Bea Black, Caldwell Police Deputy Chief Shawn Sopoaga and Advocates Against Family Violence Executive Director Kim Deugan. The gathering also heard a griping story from a young lady whose mother was killed in an act of domestic violence. A story that reminded us of the importance of hope and resilience after trauma. There are many resources available to those who may need help including Faces of Hope and the Women and Children’s Alliance WCA. www.wcaboise.org Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck signs proclamation Ada County Paramedics Chief Shawn Rayne Bea Black, WCA CEO welcomes attendees

ADA COUNTY COMMISSIONERS DESIGNATE THE WEEK OF SEPTEMBER 10-16, 2023 AS 9/11 REMEMBRANCE WEEK Each year on the somber anniversary of September 11, 2001 we pause to reflect on the events of that tragic day. Our lives were changed forever, but as a nation we remain resilient and true to our core beliefs in the goodness of humanity. Ada County Commissioners honored those who bravely worked to save lives following the terrorist attacks, with a proclamation signed on September 11, 2023. The proclamation signed by the commissioners respectfully honors those who died in New York City, Washington DC, and Pennsylvania.

5 Tour attendees gather at VRT’s Orchard Maintenance Facility, which supports all services in Ada County and houses VRT’s electric bus fleet Tour attendees visit Main Street Station’s customer waiting area, which features a bike locker, public restrooms, vending machines, and real-time arrival displays One of VRT’s 12 electric buses Main Street Station’s customer service area at the foot of the facility’s stairs and bicycle-accessible elevator; the area hosts the Customer Service desk, where riders can get route information, purchase passes, and more VALLEY REGIONAL TRANSIT OFFICIALS SHOWCASE WORK AND FACILITIES Ada County Commissioners Ryan Davidson and Tom Dayley joined Valley Regional Transit (VRT) board members and CEO Elaine Clegg on a bus tour of VRT facilities in September. The tour allowed the elected officials to see firsthand the incredible work VRT does getting people from here to there. CEO Elaine Clegg is committed to improving VRT’s services in the future. So many alternatives await us in the coming years including enhanced transit, electrification, rail service, and more. Ada County is also doing its part to reduce traffic – all Ada County employees are allowed to ride the bus free.

6 CONGRATULATIONS TO MICHELLE MOYER FOR TWENTY YEARS OF SERVICE TO ADA COUNTY Michelle started her career with Ada County in 2003 at the Barrister location of the Ada County Department of Motor Vehicles, when DMV was still located there. After a year Michelle moved to the new Meridian office. Michelle spent the next four years learning all she could about rules, codes, processes, and statutes, and in 2008 all that hard work paid off when she was promoted to lead clerk of the Meridian Branch. She spent the next seven years in that role honing her skills and expanding her expertise. In 2015, Michelle was promoted to Assistant Branch Manager. She spent most of her time at Meridian, with a short stint at the Chinden Branch in 2019. Shortly after that she made her way back to Meridian in December of 2019 where she was promoted to Branch Manager. Little did she know her first year as Manager would come with so many challenges including Covid and the new ITD GEM System. Presently Michelle oversees a very efficient, smooth-running, and customer-focused DMV Meridian Branch. Michelle, thank you for setting a great example for your Clerks every day, and for your twenty years of service to Ada County. (Pictured Left – Right) Ada County Motor Vehicle Division Manager Clayton Hall, Ada County Assessor Rebecca Arnold, Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson, DMV Branch Manager Michelle Moyer, Commission Chairman Rod Beck, Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley.
